title: In Silico Characterization of African Swine Fever Virus Nucleoprotein p10 Interaction with DNA.
authors: Istrate, Claudia; Marques, Jessica; Bule, Pedro; Correia, Silvia; Aires-da-Silva, Frederico; Duarte, Marlene; Reis, Ana Luisa; Machuqueiro, Miguel; Leitao, Alexandre; Victor, Bruno L
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟和ab initio建模表征ASFV核蛋白p10与dsDNA的结合机制，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但属于蛋白质-DNA互作的结构与动态机理研究，方法可迁移至TF-DNA建模。
abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) is the etiological agent of a highly contagious, hemorrhagic infectious swine disease, with a tremendous sanitary and economic impact on a global scale. Currently, there are no globally available vaccines or treatments. The p10 protein, a structural nucleoprotein encoded by ASFV, has been previously described as capable of binding double-stranded DNA (dsDNA), which may have implications for viral replication. However, the molecular mechanism that governs this interaction is still unknown, mostly due to the lack of a structural model for this protein. In this work, we have generated an ab initio model of the p10 protein and performed extensive structural characterization, using molecular dynamics simulations to identify the motifs and residues regulating DNA recognition. The helix-turn-helix motif identified at the C-terminal region of the protein was shown to be crucial to the dsDNA-binding efficiency. As with other DNA-binding proteins, two distinct serine and lysine-rich regions found in the two helices were identified as key players in the binding to DNA, whose importance was later validated using experimental binding assays. Altogether, these findings may contribute to a better understanding of the p10 function in ASFV replication.
abstract_zh: 非洲猪瘟病毒（ASFV）是引起一种高度传染性、出血性猪传染病的病原体，对全球范围造成巨大的卫生和经济影响。目前，全球尚无可用疫苗或治疗方法。p10蛋白，一种由ASFV编码的结构性核蛋白，此前已被描述为能够结合双链DNA（dsDNA），这可能对病毒复制具有重要意义。然而，调控这种相互作用的分子机制仍未知，主要原因是缺乏该蛋白的结构模型。在本研究中，我们生成了p10蛋白的从头计算模型，并利用分子动力学模拟进行了广泛的结构表征，以识别调控DNA识别的基序和残基。在蛋白C末端区域鉴定出的螺旋-转角-螺旋基序被证明对dsDNA结合效率至关重要。与其他DNA结合蛋白类似，两个螺旋中发现的富含丝氨酸和赖氨酸的两个不同区域被确定为与DNA结合的关键参与者，其重要性随后通过实验结合测定得到验证。总体而言，这些发现可能有助于更好地理解p10在ASFV复制中的功能。
